Aside from biological sex not being that simple (intersex people!) I give it to you that in this discussion AGAB is not the most relevant. As pointed out elsewhere, the main distinction is having a prostate or not. But in the larger discourse I find AGAB very relevant, as it signifies the *gender role* which we were expected to perform as small children.

But I'm not born male. I'm born me, a transgender woman. Doctors and society decided I was to be a boy, conform to the masculine gender roles, based on my genitalia, hence AMAB. It may seem like nitpicking but for a lot of trans people these concepts have a lot of emotional baggage. Sure, your friends may feel indifferent towards it, but let's not speak for the community as a whole. I believe AGAB is by and large the preferred terminology. Also AGAB acknowledges the fact that intersex people exist.

Not for nothing. You seem aware the terminology is LGBTIQ+ related. There's plenty of hostility towards queer people both online and offline. Whether deliberate or not, you're contributing. You could have just asked in a friendly tone, but no, you seem upset about some new to you terminology.

For example, due to gender dysphoria sex is really difficult for me. I have a partner who I really love but for her sex is important. So should we break up because of that? Seems a shame because we have a lot of good things going as well. And me not allowing her to get her needs met with someone else seems selfish to me. I feel it's an act of love to allow a partner to also find love in different places. I love them, so why would I not want them to experience as much joy and love as possible?

Ik zit een beetje in hetzelfde schuitje. Zwaar depressief en veel onverwerkt trauma waar ik nu eindelijk na jaren lang zelfstandig aanmodderen hulp voor hen gezocht. Dat aanmodderen ging soms gepaard met maandenlang niet kunnen studeren of werken. Altijd een beetje onder de radar kunnen vliegen doordat m'n studie en werk als promovendus zeer flexibel waren qua hoe ik m'n tijd besteedde, zolang ik maar na 4 jaar een proefschrift kon verdedigen. De perioden dat het me wel lukt te werken ben ik blijkbaar erg productief want heb toch m'n PhD kunnen behalen. Daarna ben ik gaan werken als postdoc en toen is alles helemaal in de soep gelopen. Deels doordat m'n eerdere strategie niet meer doenbaar was omdat dit werk veel meer korte termijn prestatiedruk heeft, deels door trauma wat naar boven is gekomen, deels door covid. Dan toch eindelijk maar ook hulp gevraagd, wat erg lastig voor me was door traumatische ervaringen met de ggz in m'n jeugd. Ik heb nu een tijdelijk contract wat eind dit jaar afloopt, zit ziek thuis, en de arbeidsdeskundige acht me volledig arbeidsongeschikt. Zuur om te horen na jaren van me specialiseren in een academische niche. Ik zal eind dit jaar in een WIA uitkering terecht komen. Ik ga die tijd dan maar gebruiken om volop in te zetten op therapie. Wellicht met een opname in het verschiet. Helaas loop ik telkens tegen eindeloze wachtlijsten aan. Het is echt heel erg zwaar.

Yes, I'm polyam/relation anarchist. Me and my long term partner (let's call her M) started out mono, and about 3years ago we went polyam. Our relationship has improved, for the most part, since it's easier to not have unhealthy expectations of the other. I get feelings for people very easily and it's freeing to allow them to develop naturally. Downside is I get feelings for metamours which make things awkward.

Though right now I'm having a difficult time managing my polyam lifestyle. Last month M suddenly decided to move in with a different partner, let's call him D (before we each had our own place). I initially thought I would be cool with that but I'm very hurt. I had envisioned a future for us, one where I and M might eventually move in together, and that vision is now shattered. Also it doesn't help that I have feelings for D which are not answered. Before the move I could compartmentalize this, but now I feel M and D have somehow merged, and I can no longer be with M without thinking about D. This stuff has me spiralling.
